name: 和奏 ぺったらぽったら本舗 (Wasou Pettara Pottara Honpo)

claims.text: Each piece is glazed and finished with a sweet soy sauce; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat, so these items are not gluten-free.
The only menu items contain oyster or conger eel plus a soy-based glaze, so there is no vegan-safe item to protect from cross-contact.
Cooking is done on a shared teppan griddle where wheat-batter okonomiyaki and wheat noodles are prepared, so cross-contact with gluten is unavoidable.
Dishes are finished with okonomiyaki sauce, which is a wheat-containing sauce, and the noodle versions use wheat soba/udon.
Everything is cooked on one griddle used for pork, egg and fish-based seasonings, with no separate vegan preparation.
No gluten-free or cross-contamination information is documented for the Hiroshima shop; the signature house granola topping may contain gluten and should be omitted by gluten-sensitive guests.
The core product is dairy Greek yogurt, so vegan guests should ask staff to build an acai-and-fruit bowl with no yogurt and no honey; no plant-milk option or dedicated vegan handling is documented.
Yogurt and acai are advertised as additive-free, with the acai described as fully organic with no artificial sweeteners.
Single shared teppan griddle used for wheat-batter okonomiyaki, wheat noodles, and tenkasu (fried wheat bits), creating heavy gluten cross-contact.
Finished with standard okonomiyaki/Carp-brand sauce, which is wheat-based; no gluten-free sauce indicated.
Okonomiyaki uses fish powder, pork belly, and egg, and the noodles are seasoned with dashi on the same griddle, so no dish is free of animal products.
Wheat noodles are boiled in shared water and the menu is entirely noodle-based, so cross-contact with gluten is unavoidable; no gluten-free preparation is offered.
The chili dipping/seasoning sauce for tsukemen and dandan noodles typically relies on wheat-containing Japanese soy sauce; no wheat-free soy sauce is indicated.
Bowls are topped with char siu pork and the sauces are meat/fish-based, so all menu items involve animal products.

name: 味処 大工町 よし村 (Ajidokoro Daikumachi Yoshimura)

claims.text: Traditional Kaga kappo cooking relies heavily on soy sauce and dashi, and the house signature jibu-ni includes fresh wheat gluten (fu) and a flour-thickened sauce, so gluten is pervasive in the kitchen.
Standard Japanese soy sauce (wheat-containing) is used throughout Kaga cuisine and its signature dishes here; no wheat-free soy sauce is documented.
The kitchen is centered on seafood and meat with dashi-based seasoning; no separate vegan preparation is documented.
Cooking is centered on Kaga local dishes such as jibuni and a range of simmered and grilled preparations that conventionally use soy sauce and dashi; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.
The menu is dominated by seafood, crab, duck and fish dashi, so vegan dishes and the avoidance of animal-based stock are not accommodated.

name: あまつぼ 柿木畠本店 (Amatsubo Kakinokibatake Honten)

claims.text: Oden centers on wheat-gluten ingredients (fu/車麸) simmered in a shared dashi pot, and the menu includes tempura and grilled items, so gluten is pervasive throughout the kitchen.
As a traditional Kaga izakaya, dishes rely on standard Japanese seasonings including soy sauce; no gluten-free tamari is documented.
The signature oden broth is made from bonito and kombu, so vegetable oden items are simmered in fish-based dashi.
